classification.difficultyReason: Students read the factored form for roots, a double-root touch point and the sign of the leading coefficient. They then eliminate wrong graphs, using the y-intercept if needed. This is a standard graph match with several simultaneous features but no calculus.

answer.worked: The zero $x=-2$ has multiplicity $1$, so the curve crosses the axis there. The zero $x=1$ has multiplicity $2$, so the curve touches the axis there. The leading term is $-x^3$, so the left end rises and the right end falls. Only graph C fits.
